overview: Italy is a great destination for students interested in construction, infrastructure development, structural design, transportation systems and sustainable urban planning. In Italy, engineering courses by universities combine scientific foundations with technical subjects, practical projects and opportunities for further specialization.

In Italy, the civil engineering bachelor's degree is normally a three-year undergraduate degree, called Laurea, with 180 ECTS credits. Students learn how to analyze, design and maintain infrastructure such as buildings, bridges, roads, railroads, water works and other civil structures .

For Indian students after Class 12, Bachelors programs in Civil Engineering in Italy can be the gateway to international engineering education. However, admission requirements, language of instruction, entrance tests, and tuition fees vary from one university to another.
Edu-Hawk Worldwide assists students in exploring university options, understanding eligibility requirements, preparing application documents and planning their study-abroad journey.

sections.title: Why Study Civil Engineering in Italy?

items: Italy has a long history of architecture, construction and infrastructure. Its universities teach engineering that includes the scientific principles and practical applications needed to understand the built environment.
Why do students consider Study Civil Engineering in Italy Bachelors programs? Here are some reasons:
Strong technical background: Study mathematics, physics, structural mechanics, construction materials and engineering design.
Infrastructure Education: Learn about bridges, buildings, transportation networks, water systems and geotechnical engineering.
Practical learning: Students may have the opportunity to engage in laboratory work, design assignments, field activities and projects, depending on the university.
International exposure: Experience the European academic environment and find out about exchange possibilities where available.
Sustainability and Innovation: Find out about infrastructure resilience, resource efficiency, and sustainable construction.
Further study possibilities: Successful graduates can apply for suitable master programs in civil, structural, environmental or related engineering fields.

Before selecting a university, students who wish to study Civil Engineering in Italy Bachelors programs should take into account the curriculum, the language of instruction, admission procedures, living costs and opportunities for practical experience.
Civil engineering undergraduate programs introduce students to the design, construction, operation and maintenance of civil structures and infrastructure.

According to the university, the curriculum may include:
Mathematics for Engineers
Physics and chemistry

Engineering drawings and graphics
Surveying & Topography
Building materials
Structural mechanics
Basics of structural engineering
Geotechnical Engineering.
Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics
Civil engineering: Transportation
Roads, railroads & airports
Water supply and drainage
Infrastructure management and construction
In case of Civil Engineering Courses in Italy, check out the official curriculum while searching as subjects, electives and credit requirements differ from institution to institution.
Popular specialization areas
Structural Engineering: The study of behavior, analysis and design of buildings, bridges and other structures.
Transportation Engineering: Deals with roads, railroads, airports and the planning of transport infrastructure.
Geotechnical Engineering: deals with the study of soil mechanics, foundations, slopes and earthworks.
Hydraulic Engineering: This is about water movement, drainage, hydraulic infrastructure and water resource systems.
Construction Engineering: concerns methods of construction, project coordination, materials and site operations.
Environmental and Infrastructure Engineering: Combines civil engineering concepts with environmental protection, resource management and sustainable infrastructure.
Some specializations are created mainly through electives or master's programs, not a dedicated undergraduate track.

sections.title: Top Universities in Italy
sections.lead: Explore top public research universities and polytechnics in Italy offering English-taught degrees, historic campuses, and generous regional scholarships.

unis.name: Politecnico di Milano, Italy
unis.desc: Politecnico di Milano, Milano Leonardo campus offers a three years bachelor's degree in Civil engineering. The university states the program language as either Italian or English, so applicants should carefully check the applicable study pathway and language requirements. This course introduces the science and engineering basis for infrastructure, covering structural mechanics, geotechnics, hydraulics, transportation systems and surveying. It might appeal to students seeking an engineering-oriented university in Milan with a pathway to postgraduate study. Official course page: https://www.polimi.it/en/education/laurea-programmes/programme-detail/civil-engineering 2 . Politecnico di Torino - Civil and Environmental Engineering This is a separate 3 year bachelor's program taught fully in English for the above mentioned program structure. It blends fundamentals of civil engineering with environmental issues such as resource management and waste-treatment systems. Students study the scientific bases before moving on to subjects related to structures, geotechnics, surveying, transportation and environmental engineering. This option may be of special interest to international applicants looking for an English taught undergraduate pathway in infrastructure and environmental sustainability. Official course page: https://www.polito.it/en/education/bachelor-s-degree-programmes/civil-and-environmental-engineering 3 . University of Bologna For the academic year 2026/27 the University of Bologna is offering a three-year bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering at the Bologna campus. The program consists of 180 ECTS credits and is taught in Italian. The published admission information includes open access through the TOLC-I procedure; applicants should check the relevant requirements and any conditions attached to enrollment. The curriculum provides a foundation in civil engineering and enables progression to further study in related disciplines. Official course page: https://www.unibo.it/en/insegnamenti/corsi-di-laurea-magistrale/6667

unis.name: Who can apply for Civil Engineering in Italy?
unis.desc: Indian applicants should meet the academic and admission requirements prescribed by the university of choice. Education Applicants typically need: A recognized secondary school qualification, e.g. Class 12 or equivalent. An acceptable qualification for entry to university for undergraduate study in Italy. Mathematics and other subjects relevant to the program. Academic results to meet any stated selection criteria. Additional qualification verification documents as may be required. The universities assess the foreign qualifications on the basis of their own admission rules and of the Italian requirements in force. Class 12 pass is not the only criteria for admission. Subject requirements Civil engineering requires mathematics because the curriculum includes calculations, mechanics, structural analysis and engineering design. Physics is also important to understand forces, motion, materials and behavior of infrastructure. Applicants should check that the university they are applying to has not set any subject prerequisites or minimum academic scores. Language requirements Language requirements vary depending on the program: Degrees taught in Italian: Applicants may need to demonstrate their Italian language proficiency. English taught degrees: Applicants may be required to provide accepted proof of English language. Mixed-language pathways: Students should check if any further language requirements are added in later years. Entrance exams Some universities have an engineering entrance test or some other procedure of selection. For example, the University of Bologna offers TOLC-I for its Civil Engineering bachelor's program. Other institutions may have other requirements. Students planning to do their Bachelors in Civil Engineering in Ital y may visit the official university website to get information on the latest examination syllabus, registration deadlines, selection criteria and accepted alternatives.

7. How to Apply for Civil Engineering in Italy
Students can apply to Italian universities in general using the following steps.
Select Your Engineering Focus: What are you most passionate about-structural engineering, transportation, construction, hydraulics, or environmental infrastructure?
Shortlist universities: Compare course structure, language of instruction, tuition, and location.
Check eligibility: Make sure your Class 12 qualification and subjects meet the university's requirements.
Prepare for entrance exams: Know which test is applicable to you, and check the syllabus and application deadlines.
Gather Documentation Collect academic transcripts, passport, proof of language and any other documents needed to verify your qualifications.
University Application Submission: Fill in the official application and selection procedures.
Find out the status of your admission: Follow the instructions given by the university to accept the offer and complete the enrollment process.
Complete pre-enrolment if required International students applying for an Italian study visa normally complete the applicable procedure through Universitaly.
Apply for the student visa Submit the documents required by the competent Italian diplomatic mission. Admission is not a guaranty that a visa will be issued to you.
Plan accommodation and travel: Arrange housing, insurance and arrival arrangements before you leave.
Application dates and procedures vary depending on institution, applicant category and intake. Students must adhere to the latest official university and visa instructions.

sections.title: Acknowledgment, Further Reading and Professional Requirements

items: A bachelor's degree in civil engineering can be a stepping stone to technical employment and further education. Professional requirements vary depending on country, job and desired responsibilities.
Further education: Graduates may apply for suitable master's programs if they fulfilll the admission requirements.
Engineering jobs: Employers may look for technical knowledge, project experience, software skills and hands-on training.

Professional practice in Italy Certain independent professional activities require the relevant professional examination and registration. Information on these requirements is published by Politecnico di Milano and Politecnico di Torino for their graduates.
Employment in India: Graduates should check the requirements of the employer, role and any relevant professional authority.
International career plans: rules on recognition, work authorization and professional registration can vary from country to country.
Students should review the degree program prior to enrollment to ensure that it is consistent with their desired career path.
9. Career Options After Civil Engineering in Italy
Graduates may pursue careers in construction, infrastructure, transportation, structural design, surveying, water management and engineering consultancy.
Possible starting positions are:
Civil Engineer Junior
Site Engineer (Graduate)
Structural Assistant Engineer
Construction Project Assistant
Assistant Quantity Surveyor
Junior Transport Engineer
Assistant Surveyor
Geotechnical Engineer Assistant
Water Resources Assistant Engineer
Infrastructure Planning Aide
CAD Tech
Coordinator, Building & Construction
Industries hiring civil engineering graduates
Construction and real estate: Residential, commercial and industrial construction.
Development of infrastructure: Bridges, highways, railroads, tunnels and public infrastructure.
Structural engineering: Analysis, design and assessment of structures under the supervision or responsibility arrangements required for the role.
Transport: Road networks, rail systems and transport infrastructure planning.
Water and environmental systems: water supply, drainage, flood protection and environmental infrastructure.
Engineering consultancy: Technical drawings, design support, project documentation and engineering analysis.
International applicants may need to submit all or some of the following documents:
Valid passport.
Class 10 certificate and marksheet.
Class 12 marksheet & certificate.
School-leaving certificate (SSL)
The university requested academic transcripts and other school records.
Score on entrance exam (if applicable).
Proof of English or Italian language skills, if required.
Official translation of academic documents upon request.
Copies of qualification verification documents (if necessary).
Submitted university application.
Letter of admission or enrollment papers.
Proof of financial means, accommodation and insurance as required for the visa.
Any other documents required by the university or consular authority.
The final checklist depends on the university, applicant's qualifications and applicable visa procedures. Follow the official requirements for your selected program and intake.

faq.question: Can Indian students do civil engineering in Italy after 12?
faq.answer: "Yeah. Indian students are eligible to apply provided their Class 12 qualification meets the university's entry requirements and they satisfy the relevant academic, language, entrance-test and document requirements.

faq.question: What is the length of a bachelor's degree in civil engineering in Italy?
faq.answer: In Italy, civil engineering bachelor's degrees are normally three years long and total 180 ECTS credits. Students should verify the length and format of the program they have selected.

faq.question: Are there bachelor's courses in civil engineering taught in English in Italy?
faq.answer: Some programs or pathways are available in English, others are taught in Italian. For instance, Politecnico di Torino offers a separate Civil and Environmental Engineering bachelor's program in English. Please check the full teaching language of the degree before applying.

faq.question: What are the fees for civil engineers in Italy?
faq.answer: Roughly speaking, for planning purposes, you can expect to pay between approximately €900 and €4,000 per year for public university tuition, although private institutions may charge more. Actual fees depend on the institution, program and fee rules applicable.

faq.answer: Based on your skills and experience, you could look into jobs in construction, infrastructure, surveying, transportation, structural engineering support, water systems and engineering consultancy. Some graduates go on to a master's degree for further specialization.
